brief: A 9-second news intro: a red banner wipes in from the left with 'BREAKING' in bold white on it; then a ticker along the bottom scrolls 'Markets rally - Tech leads gains - Oil steady' continuously from right to left; meanwhile a clock in the top-right corner shows 10:42 with a blinking colon.
checks: Does a red banner wipe in from the left edge of the frame (starting off‑screen left and ending fully inside)?
Does the banner contain the word **BREAKING** in bold white text (centered on the banner)?
Does the ticker at the bottom begin to scroll only after the banner’s wipe‑in animation has finished?
Does the ticker continuously display the exact phrase "Markets rally - Tech leads gains - Oil steady" (repeating without alteration)?
Does the ticker scroll smoothly from right to left at a steady pace with no pauses, reversals, or jumps?
Is a clock visible in the top‑right corner for the entire duration of the intro?
Does the clock show the time **10:42** (hours:minutes) throughout the video?
Does the colon in the clock blink on and off at a regular interval (approximately 0.5 s on, 0.5 s off)?
During the banner wipe‑in, does no visual element touch or cross the outer frame edge (the banner starts off‑screen but ends fully inside)?
Does the banner’s wipe‑in animation ease in and out (i.e., it starts slow, speeds up, then slows) rather than moving at a constant speed?
Is there at least one visible change (movement, color shift, or blink) in every second of the video, ensuring no dead air?
Does the final frame remain static for at least half a second before the video ends?
Are the colors harmonious – specifically, does the red banner provide strong contrast with the white ‘BREAKING’ text without any clashing hues elsewhere?
Are there any visible glitches, flicker, overlapping text, or rendering artifacts in the video?
